setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Nothing else exists yet: no second pattern, no scale change, no second channel and one song slot. Trig merge modes decide what happens when two patterns on one channel both have a trig on a step: Skip (the default) drops those steps, Only keeps only those steps, and All keeps every step.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Do these in order. 1) Tap Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 2 at (2,1) and tap steps 1 and 3 on Pattern Trig. 2) Tap Pattern (5,8) again for Pattern Note and raise step 1 to (1,3) and step 3 to (3,1): degrees 4 and 6. 3) Tap Scale (4,8), tap slot 2 at (2,3), turn E2 to Root and E3 two detents up to D, then press K3: D major is applied. 4) Tap Channel (3,8) and tap pattern slot (2,2) to assign pattern 2 to channel 1 beside pattern 1. 5) Press Play, then Stop. Skip drops steps 1 and 3, where both patterns have a trig, so only steps 2 and 4 play: E and G of D major (MIDI 64 and 67) at velocities 117 and 97.
steps.title: Build pattern 2 and hear Skip

steps.caption: Tap the trig merge button (14,8) twice to move from Skip through Only to All. The button lights at medium brightness.
steps.title: Move the trig merge to All

steps.caption: Hold the velocity merge button (16,8) and tap pattern 1 at (1,2) to take velocities from pattern 1, then press Play and Stop. All four steps play. Steps 2 and 4 come from pattern 1 alone (E and G, 64 and 67). Steps 1 and 3 have a trig in both patterns, so their notes are the average of the two patterns' scale degrees: step 1 averages D (degree 0) and A (degree 4) to F# (66), and step 3 averages F# and C# to A (69). The result is MIDI 66, 64, 69, 67 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97.
steps.title: Merge all, with pattern 1 velocities

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1), turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device and press K3. The Device page now reads CH02.
steps.title: Select channel 2

steps.caption: On the Device page choose the same device on MIDI port 2 and MIDI channel 2 (turn E3 or E2 to each setting) and press K3 to apply. Tap pattern slot (2,2) for pattern 2, hold step 1 and tap step 4 to give channel 2 the range steps 1-4, then turn E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Masks and press K3. The screen reads Note Masks for CH02.
steps.title: Route channel 2 and open its Masks

steps.caption: On Masks, hold step 3 and play MIDI note 76 at velocity 90 on a MIDI keyboard or controller to lock it to that step. Tap channel 1 at (1,1) and press Play, then Stop. Both channels sound, each on its own port: channel 1 plays 66, 64, 69, 67 as before, and channel 2 plays pattern 2: MIDI 69 (A) on step 1 and your 76 on step 3.
steps.title: Add a keyboard note to channel 2

steps.caption: Do these in order. 1) Tap Song (6,8) and set the global length to 4 steps: tap (2,7), which sets 1, then (8,7) three times. 2) Copy slot 1 to slot 2: hold slot (1,1) and tap (2,1), then tap (2,1) to select slot 2. 3) Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave-up (11,8), so slot 2 plays an octave higher. 4) Tap Song (6,8), select slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play. The four-step phrase plays, then repeats an octave higher in slot 2: MIDI 66, 64, 69, 67, then 78, 76, 81, 79 on channel 1, while channel 2 plays its A and 76 in both slots.
steps.title: Copy slot 1 to slot 2 an octave up

title: Build two channels: merge patterns, route a second part and chain slots
